# Slack Pro vs Microsoft Teams Essentials — 50-person software company (August 2026)

Cited from the six most authoritative official Slack and Microsoft pages reachable in the budget. Cells the cited pages do not disclose are marked **Unknown** (no inference).

| Decision field | **Slack Pro** | **Microsoft Teams Essentials** |
|---|---|---|
| **Price / currency / cadence / unit** | $8.75 USD per active user/month (monthly billing) or $7.25 USD per active user/month (annual billing) [1] | $4.00 per user/month, paid yearly (annual subscription, auto-renews) on the US Essentials landing page [2] |
| **Meeting participant limit** | Unknown — the official Slack plans-and-features page in scope does not state a per-huddle/participant cap for Pro [3] | Unknown — the cited Essentials landing page, QuickStart guide, and Teams service description do not disclose a participant cap for the Essentials SKU [2] [4] [5] |
| **Meeting duration limit** | Unknown — same Slack plans-and-features page does not state a duration cap for Pro [3] | Unknown — not disclosed on the cited Microsoft Essentials pages [2] [4] [5] |
| **Guest / external collaboration** | Guest accounts are a paid-plan feature (Pro qualifies). Two roles: **Multi-Channel Guests** (charged as full members, can join unlimited specified channels) and **Single-Channel Guests** (free, one channel each, capped at 5 single-channel guests per paid active member). **Slack Connect** for cross-organization channels. Workspace owners/admins approve invitations and govern access. | Unknown — the cited Microsoft pages describe Essentials as a standalone Teams subscription for meetings/chat/collaboration but do not surface a guest/external policy in scope [2] [4] [5] |
| **Security / admin controls** | Pro is covered by ISO 27001 and ISO 27018 certifications. Admin/security features referenced on the plans-and-features page include administrators, access logs, approving apps, channel management, and analytics. [1] [3] | Unknown — the cited Essentials and service-description pages do not enumerate an admin/security control set for the standalone Essentials SKU [2] [4] [5] |

## Recommendation — external client collaboration

**Slack Pro is the better-documented fit** purely on what the cited official pages disclose. Its guest model is explicit and granular (paid Multi-Channel Guests, free Single-Channel Guests capped at 5 per paid seat, plus Slack Connect for cross-company channels), all governed by workspace owner/admin approval. The cited Microsoft pages do not surface an equivalent guest/external-collaboration policy for the standalone Teams Essentials SKU within this budget. Teams Essentials' lower per-seat price (~$4 vs $7.25–$8.75) is officially confirmed, so if guest richness is secondary to cost, that would warrant re-checking the Microsoft pages first.

## What remains unconfirmed within the 6-URL budget

- Pro **huddle participant cap** and **duration cap** (Slack plans-and-features page in scope does not state them).
- Teams Essentials **meeting participant cap**, **duration cap**, and **guest/external policy** (Essentials landing page, QuickStart, and service description snippets in scope do not surface them).
- **Detailed admin/security** feature matrix for the standalone Teams Essentials SKU (e.g., audit logs, Conditional Access, SCIM) — not enumerated on the cited Microsoft pages.

To close these gaps without exceeding the budget, a follow-up read of the Teams Premium / Microsoft 365 business comparison page and a deeper read of the Microsoft Teams service description would be the highest-yield next sources.

---
